model_annotation: The bar chart displays the effect sizes for various language families and groups, categorized by language family on the horizontal axis (including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic) and the effect on the vertical axis, which ranges from 0 to 30. Each category contains a set of colored bars representing different language pairs or components: XLM-L2 (light blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light red), and XLM-B2 (dark red). Error bars indicate the variability or confidence intervals for each measurement. The data show that the IE-Indic family has the highest effect sizes, particularly for XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, and XLM-R2, with values exceeding 20. In contrast, the Isolate and Uralic categories generally exhibit the lowest effect sizes, mostly below 5. The XLM-B2 (dark red) bars are consistently among the highest in most categories, especially in IE-Indic and Semitic, where they reach values above 20. The mBERT-B2 (light red) bars also show relatively high values in IE-Indic and Semitic. The XLM-L2 (light blue) bars show moderate effects across most families, with notable peaks in IE-Indic and Semitic. The mBERT-R2 (light green) and XLM-R2 (dark green) bars generally show lower effects, with some exceptions in IE-Indic. The chart illustrates that effect sizes vary significantly across language families and models, with the IE-Indic family showing the most pronounced differences.
